title: Dedicated provisioning dashboard + alerts for time-to-ready (stage breakdown)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Build a single "time-to-ready" dashboard for Dedicated pool provisioning runs with stage breakdown + define alert thresholds for (1) stuck stages and (2) elevated failure rates.

Context
Provision-to-ready automation is rolling out with a staged state machine (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed). SRE needs:
- a reliable p50/p95 view by stage to enforce stage budgets
- a fast drilldown path from "pool is late" → "which stage" → "why" (logs/events + correlation_id)
- alerting that is actionable (avoids paging on expected slow runs / single-customer edge cases)

Links
- Confluence spec: /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dedicated-readiness-dashboard-spec
- Confluence metrics/alerting definitions: /eng-sre/operational-tooling/time-to-ready-metrics-and-alerting
- PR (dashboards/alerts): sources/github/observability-pack/pr-1204
- PR (telemetry + naming/cardinality): sources/github/redwood/pr-48239
- PR (structured provisioning events + correlation_id): sources/github/redwood/pr-48232
- Runbook: /eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-pool-provisioning-runbook

What shipped
1) Dashboard: "Dedicated Provisioning — Time-to-Ready"
Primary audience: Infra Fleet operators + SRE oncall. Secondary: Platform/control-plane during pilots.

Key dashboard sections/widgets
A. Overview (top row)
- Time-to-ready p50/p95 by region (last 7d) + delta vs previous 7d
- Total runs, success rate, failure rate (last 24h / 7d)
- "Runs currently in-flight" count + breakdown by stage
- Fast filter pills: env (prod/staging), region, GPU SKU, pool_id (limited), customer_id (limited)

B. Stage breakdown
- Stacked bar: average time-to-ready split by stage (p50 + p95 selectable)
- Stage duration histograms (one per stage, with shared axes):
  - Provisioning
  - Imaging
  - Bootstrapping
  - Validating
- Heatmap: stage duration by region x SKU (p95)

C. Failure analysis
- Failed runs by stage (count) + failure rate per stage (ratio)
- Top failure reasons (from normalized error_category):
  - iam_permission
  - quota
  - artifact_mirror
  - dns_tls
  - gpu_health
  - helm_values
  - perf_canary_regression
- Table: latest failures (last 50) with columns:
  - started_at, pool_id, region, sku, stage, error_category, correlation_id, links
  - links: logs search, run details endpoint, runbook anchor

D. In-flight / stuck detection view (operator)
- Table: all runs in non-terminal state with "time in current stage" and a red/yellow indicator based on stage budget
- Drilldown links (built from correlation_id):
  - logs explorer query
  - provisioning run details endpoint
  - runbook section for the current stage

Dashboard implementation notes
- We intentionally did not default to pool_id/customer_id filters in queries to avoid high-cardinality blowups. Pool/customer drilldowns are via table panels that query recent runs only (time-bounded) and include correlation_id for direct debugging.
- "Top N pools" views are time-bounded (24h) and use table queries rather than aggregations over long windows.

Metric/query contracts assumed (from ENG-2748 + PR-48239)
- Histogram: redwood.provisioning.time_to_ready_seconds{env,region,result}
- Histogram: redwood.provisioning.stage_duration_seconds{env,region,stage,result}
- Counter: redwood.provisioning.stage_transitions_total{env,region,from_stage,to_stage,result}
- Counter: redwood.provisioning.failures_total{env,region,stage,error_category}
- Gauge: redwood.provisioning.runs_in_flight{env,region,stage}
- Event/log field: correlation_id (required), pool_id (best effort), customer_id (best effort)

2) Alerts
We agreed on a two-tier model:
- Paging only for broad/systemic breakages (multiple runs, sustained impact)
- Ticket/Slack notifications for single-run or small-burst issues, so operators can triage without waking oncall unnecessarily

Alert definitions (initial thresholds; will revisit after 2 weeks of data)
A. Stuck stage (ticket by default; page when widespread)
A1. "ProvisioningRunStuckStage" (creates ticket + posts to #eng-infra)
Trigger:
- Any run appears to be in-flight in a stage longer than the stage budget * 2, sustained for 30m
- Minimum in-flight runs: >= 1
Routing:
- Ticket to Infra Fleet (Fleet provisioning) with labels: provisioning, stuck-stage
Payload includes: stage, region, approx time in stage, top correlation_id examples, dashboard link

A2. "ProvisioningRunStuckStage_Widespread" (pages SRE)
Trigger:
- In-flight runs >= 3 stuck in the same stage AND stage budget * 2 exceeded for >= 30m
OR
- In-flight runs >= 5 across any stages exceeding stage budget * 3 for >= 30m
Routing:
- Page SRE oncall; auto-post to #eng-sre and #eng-infra

Stage budget baseline (used for indicator bands; sourced from baseline analysis + sprint kickoff)
- Provisioning: 30m (warn at 45m; critical at 60m)
- Imaging: 45m (warn at 70m; critical at 90m)
- Bootstrapping: 30m (warn at 45m; critical at 60m)
- Validating: 25m (warn at 40m; critical at 50m)
Note: budgets are for the automation path; manual pauses should exclude time-in-stage (handled via run state "Paused" which stops the timer).

B. High failure rate (systemic)
B1. "ProvisioningStageFailureRateHigh" (ticket + Slack)
Trigger:
- failures_total / stage_transitions_total > 20% for a given stage over 60m
- Minimum denominator: stage_transitions_total >= 5
Routing:
- Ticket to owning team based on stage:
  - Provisioning/Imaging: Infra Fleet
  - Bootstrapping/Validating: SRE (with control-plane CC if validation failures are API/auth related)

B2. "ProvisioningStageFailureRateCritical" (pages SRE)
Trigger:
- failures_total / stage_transitions_total > 50% for a given stage over 30m
- Minimum denominator: stage_transitions_total >= 10

C. Data quality / monitoring integrity
C1. "TimeToReadyMetricsMissing" (ticket)
Trigger:
- runs_in_flight > 0 but no stage_duration_seconds samples for 15m in the same env/region
Rationale: catches broken telemetry wiring early; should not page.

Open questions resolved
- Paging vs ticketing for stuck stages: agreed to ticket by default, page only on widespread patterns (see A2). This matches the #eng-sre thread outcome and reduces noise during pilots.
- Pool/customer filtering: keep long-window panels low-cardinality; provide pool/customer drilldowns via recent-runs tables + correlation_id links.

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard loads in <10s for default view (prod, last 7d) and does not time out.
- Stage duration widgets show meaningful p50/p95 and reflect known slow imaging region from pilot data.
- Alerts are wired to correct oncall rotations / ticket project and include direct dashboard + runbook links.
- At least one synthetic "stuck" scenario validated in staging (manual test run that holds a stage open beyond critical).

Test plan / validation
- Staging: forced a provisioning run to pause in Bootstrapping; verified:
  - stuck-stage table shows >critical indicator
  - ticket-style alert fired to #eng-infra within expected delay window
- Prod (shadow): alerts enabled with "notify only" for first 48h post-rollout; then paging policy enabled for A2/B2.

Rollout notes

- Revisit thresholds after we have 2 weeks of automated runs (especially Imaging p95 by region/SKU).
